std-agent-completion.name: std-agent-completion
std-agent-completion.description: Wraps llm/generate — takes a prompt, returns generated text.

std-agent-context.name: std-agent-context
std-agent-context.description: std-agent-context — keeps what an in-app assistant sends the model bounded. COMPACT { messages } passes a conversation of at most `keepMessages` turns straight through as COMPACTED; a longer one has its older turns summarized with `call-service llm summarize` into one leading note and keeps the last `keepMessages` turns verbatim. If summarizing fails, the older turns are dropped and the recent ones still go through, with a visible warning — a summarizer outage never blocks the assistant. Headless. Nothing is persisted: the conversation itself lives in std-agent-session.

std-agent-fix-loop.name: std-agent-fix-loop
std-agent-fix-loop.description: Agent fix loop — evaluate a program and, when it does not validate, ask the model for a repair. VALIDATE_PROGRAM { program } runs `program/eval` (the 0-error / 0-warning gate, written to the workspace's orbitals/ on success): a valid program emits PROGRAM_VALID { behavior }; an invalid one hands the validator's issues to `call-service llm generate` and emits FIX_PROPOSED { issues, fix } with the model's repair instructions. Headless apart from a status line.
std-agent-fix-loop.statePattern: failed, fixed, fixing, idle, valid, validating
std-agent-fix-loop.capabilities: program repair, fix validation errors, evaluate a program, repair suggestion

std-agent-memory.name: std-agent-memory
std-agent-memory.description: std-agent-memory — what an in-app assistant remembers across conversations. Owns AgentMemory rows (content + its embedding, ownerId = the real @user). RECALL { messages } embeds the last turn with `call-service llm embed`, ranks the stored memories whose embedding is comparable (same length as the query's) by cosine similarity and emits RECALLED { messages, context } with the closest `recallLimit` memories joined into one context string (empty when nothing is stored); if embedding fails it emits RECALLED with an empty context, so a memory outage never blocks the assistant. REMEMBER { reply } stores the exchange it just recalled for (asked + answered) with its embedding. AgentMemoryRecall is headless (failures show as toasts); AgentMemoryBrowse is the list view. Rows are meant to be private to their owner: the binding organism declares the @read scoping.

std-agent-planner.name: std-agent-planner
std-agent-planner.description: Agent planner molecule — recall memories, then generate a plan from the prompt + recalled context.

std-agent-pool.name: std-agent-pool
std-agent-pool.description: std-agent-pool — a shared pool of generated behaviors that every user of the app draws from. WRITE { value, name, kind, topic, fields, description } takes a behavior already built and validated (a `program/eval` result), keeps its source durably (`behavior/source` → `program/print` → the `storage` service; the provider is the deployment's), embeds its description (`llm embed`) and records a PoolEntry; any failure on the way leaves no entry (WRITE_FAILED). SEARCH { vector, kinds, exclude, take } ranks the live entries of this pool by cosine similarity to the vector, nudged by their quality, and answers POOL_FOUND with the best ones, no model call. SIGNAL { id, signal } counts a play, like, hide, right or wrong answer on an entry and retires it once it has been played enough and most of its outcomes are hides or wrong answers. The pool name, kinds, bucket and key prefix and the quality knobs are config, so the same mechanism serves any app that pools generated behaviors.
std-agent-pool.capabilities: behavior pool, shared generated content, retrieve by meaning, reuse generated behaviors, quality signals, retire bad content

std-agent-proposal.name: std-agent-proposal
std-agent-proposal.description: std-agent-proposal — an agent that reads what the person hands over, works out a structured proposal, and commits nothing until they approve it. The app starts it with PROPOSAL_REQUESTED { input, context } (any trait emitting it, or the person typing into the start form when `showInputForm` is on). A second std-agent-tool-loop answers with `instructions`, `prompt` and `tools` as the signed-in person — `quiet`, its reply and failure renamed PROPOSAL_LOOP_REPLIED / PROPOSAL_LOOP_FAILED so they never reach the assistant's chat — and submits its proposal through one declared input, PROPOSE (its @description is the tool text): a summary and a list of items, each a flat map of scalar values the app names. The person reviews it (the summary, the items drawn with `itemPattern` and `itemFields`) and chooses: Approve emits PROPOSAL_APPROVED { proposal } for the app to commit (the app owns the commit; this atom writes nothing); Revise sends their written feedback back to the agent, which proposes again; Discard emits PROPOSAL_DISCARDED. Cancel while the agent works aborts its model call and emits PROPOSAL_CANCELLED. A run that fails, or ends without proposing, shows its error with Retry and Discard. The panel renders into `panelSlot`. Import the orbital once per app: `orbital Proposal = Proposal.orbitals.AgentProposalOrbital { config { instructions: "…", prompt: "…", itemFields: […] } }`, restating `tools` with PROPOSE addressed by its local orbital name (`{ event: Proposal.AgentProposalWorkflow.PROPOSE }`). Instructions, prompts, item fields and labels are the app's vocabulary, declared in config.
std-agent-proposal.capabilities: agent proposal, review before commit, human approval of agent output, approve or revise agent suggestions, structured proposal review, ai drafts for approval, extract then confirm

std-agent-session.name: std-agent-session
std-agent-session.description: std-agent-session — the conversation with an in-app assistant. AgentThread owns the persisted AgentMessage rows (role, content, ownerId stamped with the real @user, createdAt): SEND stores the user's message, reloads the thread and emits CONVERSE with the whole conversation, oldest first, for std-agent-tool-loop to answer; REPLIED stores the reply. AgentConversation is what the user sees, in the browser: the thread as chat bubbles with every step the assistant takes interleaved live (STEP: each model call, each tool it used and what the app answered), a thinking row while it works, and a chat bar. The two talk over the assistant contract, from any orbital: AgentConversation emits ASSISTANT_SEND and hears AgentMessagesLoaded, ASSISTANT_THREAD_FAILED, ASSISTANT_STEP, ASSISTANT_REPLIED and ASSISTANT_REPLY_FAILED; AgentThread hears ASSISTANT_SEND. So a conversation placed on any section's page reaches the app's one assistant (std-agent-assistant) with no wiring. Rows are meant to be private to their owner: owner-scoped access needs an [identity] roster, so the binding organism declares the @read/@create scoping on AgentMessage — this generic atom cannot.

std-agent-suggestions.name: std-agent-suggestions
std-agent-suggestions.description: std-agent-suggestions — an agent that proactively proposes things to the signed-in person, who accepts or dismisses each one. The agent proposes through one declared input, PROPOSE_SUGGESTION (its @description is the tool text): a kind, a title, a body that gives its reasoning, an optional action (a name the app routes) with a payload, an optional href, and a subject (what it is about). A suggestion's signature is kind:action:subject; a signature that was ever proposed to this person, accepted or dismissed included, is never stored again (SUGGESTION_DUPLICATE), and no more than `maxPending` wait at once (SUGGESTION_LIMIT_REACHED). `kinds` and `actions`, when listed, are the only values accepted (SUGGESTION_REJECTED). The agent runs on its own: any trait emitting SUGGESTIONS_TRIGGERED (or an app event routed into AgentSuggestionTrigger's TRIGGERED by re-binding that trait in the import body with `omit { AgentSuggestionTrigger }` and its own `listens`) asks for a run, and once `cooldownMinutes` have passed since this person's last run a second std-agent-tool-loop answers `prompt` with `tools` as the signed-in person — `quiet`, so it streams no live steps and toasts no failure, and its reply and failure are renamed PROACTIVE_REPLIED / PROACTIVE_FAILED so they never reach the assistant's chat. AgentSuggestionInbox lists the pending suggestions with Accept and Dismiss and an empty state that offers to look again (SUGGESTIONS_ANALYZE_REQUESTED). Accept stores accepted, emits SUGGESTION_ACCEPTED { action, payload, href, … } for the app to route (and navigates to `href` when the suggestion has one); Dismiss stores dismissed and emits SUGGESTION_DISMISSED. The inbox renders into `panelSlot`: `main` inline (the content of a std-panel-launcher), or `modal`/`drawer` opened with OPEN and closed with CLOSE (set std-app-layout's notificationClickEvent, or a topBarActions event, to SUGGESTIONS_OPEN_REQUESTED). Import the orbital once per app: `orbital Suggestions = Suggest.orbitals.AgentSuggestionsOrbital { entity MySuggestion  entities { AgentSuggestionRun: MySuggestionRun } config { … } }`, retargeting the records onto owner-scoped entities (`ownerId` a relation to your [identity] roster, with @read/@create/@update); a suggestion's proposer, inbox and trigger read only the rows whose ownerId is the signed-in person. PROPOSE_SUGGESTION's refusals (SUGGESTION_DUPLICATE, SUGGESTION_LIMIT_REACHED, SUGGESTION_REJECTED) are the agent's tool response; no trait listens to them. Suggestion kinds, actions and prompts are the app's vocabulary, declared in config.
std-agent-suggestions.capabilities: proactive suggestions, agent recommendations, suggestion inbox, next best action, accept or dismiss suggestions, notification bell suggestions, agent proposals

std-agent-tool-call.name: std-agent-tool-call
std-agent-tool-call.description: Wraps llm/call-tools — takes messages + tools, returns tool-call result.

std-agent-tool-loop.name: std-agent-tool-loop
std-agent-tool-loop.description: std-agent-tool-loop — answers a conversation by operating the running app as the caller, through `call-service llm call-tools`. Its `tools` are `{ scope: declared }` (every declared external input plus a read over every persisted entity), or named declared inputs (addressed like a listens source: `Trait.EVENT`, `Orbital.Trait.EVENT`) and entities to read; each input fires as the signed-in user through the ordinary dispatch (guards and entity policies apply) and each read returns only the rows the caller may read. Headless: the conversation UI (std-agent-session) shows the reply; a failure shows as a toast, unless `quiet` is on (a background run nobody is watching: no live steps and no toast). CONVERSE carries the conversation (and optionally what std-agent-memory recalled); ASSISTANT_STEP carries each step live while it works (a model call, a tool it used, what the app answered) to the asking tab; ASSISTANT_REPLIED carries the reply, every step and the token usage; ASSISTANT_REPLY_FAILED carries the error. These names are the assistant contract std-agent-session's conversation hears from any orbital. Compose with std-agent-session (the conversation) and std-agent-trace (the step record).

std-agent-trace.name: std-agent-trace
std-agent-trace.description: std-agent-trace — the persisted record of what an in-app assistant did. Each REPLIED (from std-agent-tool-loop) stores one AgentRun row: the reply, every step (each model call, each tool used with its arguments, whether it took effect and why not), the tokens and the model calls; each REPLY_FAILED stores a failed run with its error. The record verification grades and later optimisation reads, in one format for tests and production. AgentTraceRecorder is headless; AgentRunBrowse is the run list. Rows carry ownerId (the real @user); the binding organism scopes @read.

eval-agent-builder.name: eval-agent-builder
eval-agent-builder.description: Eval of std-agent-builder's ladder over std-agent-pool. RUN_CASE { index } builds the case's request through the ladder (the pool first, adopted at or above its threshold; otherwise a std learning instrument filled by the model with its knobs and a one-line hint), pools what was built, and records an EvalCase: the tier that served it, the behavior, the hint, the latency and the verdict: the tier the case expects, with a hint. Driven from outside, one case at a time.

std-agent-assistant.name: std-agent-assistant
std-agent-assistant.description: std-agent-assistant — an in-app assistant that operates the running app for the signed-in user. Each section's floating button opens it in a side panel docked beside the page (std-panel-launcher; a side sheet on small screens), where the conversation shows every step the assistant takes live as it works; /assistant is the same conversation as a full page, in the app's own shell (pass `appName` and `navItems`); past conversations and what the assistant remembers open in place from its toolbar (Back returns to the chat), on either surface. One request flows down a chain of std agent atoms on the bus: the conversation (std-agent-session) SENDs → CONVERSE → std-agent-context bounds it → std-agent-memory adds what it recalls → std-agent-tool-loop answers it through `call-service llm call-tools`, firing only the inputs and reading only the entities its `tools` allow, as the signed-in user → ASSISTANT_REPLIED goes back to the conversation, to memory (remembered) and to std-agent-trace (the run record). By default the tools are the program's own declarations: every `-> external` input (its @description is the tool text) and a read over every persisted entity, so composing building blocks composes the assistant's abilities. Any section's page gets the assistant with two traits, `XAssistant = AgentSession.traits.AgentConversation` and a std-panel-launcher dock: the conversation speaks the ASSISTANT_* contract from any orbital, so the assistant needs no per-section wiring. Import the orbital once per app: `orbital Assistant = Agent.orbitals.AgentAssistantOrbital { config { instructions: "…" } }`. The conversation, memory and run records live in AgentRecordsOrbital; retarget them onto your own owner-scoped entities (`ownerId` a relation to your [identity] roster, with @read/@create) with `entities { AgentMessage: …, AgentMemory: …, AgentRun: …, AgentChat: … }`. The conversation is kept across pages and reloads (each person's most recently used conversation is the current one);

std-agent-builder.name: std-agent-builder
std-agent-builder.description: Agent builder — turns a request into a behavior by walking a ladder of caching tiers, cheapest first. START { request, orbitalName, context } embeds the request (`call-service llm embed`) and walks `ladder`: each step ranks its source by cosine similarity — installed behaviors under its registry folders (`behavior/catalog`), or a pool (POOL_SEARCH, answered by POOL_FOUND from std-agent-pool) — and when the best match reaches the step's threshold runs the step's action, otherwise goes to the next step. Actions: `mount` builds a page around the best match's first trait (`program/eval`); `adopt` serves the best match as it is, no model call; `fill` describes the best match (`behavior/describe`), asks the model once to set its knobs and the extra `fillFields`, applies them (`behavior/apply`) and evaluates the result (`program/eval`, final), feeding validator issues back for up to `maxRepairs` repair turns. BUILD_PROGRESS streams each step; BUILD_COMPLETE { orbitalName, behavior, value, tier, fields } carries the behavior and the step that served it; BUILD_REJECTED { error, errors } follows an exhausted ladder or a failed build. The default ladder mounts the closest UI molecule, as earlier versions did.
std-agent-builder.statePattern: building, choosing, describing, done, failed, filling, idle, searching
std-agent-builder.capabilities: build a behavior from a request, caching tiers, retrieve before generating, adopt an existing behavior, fill a behavior's knobs, pick a behavior by meaning, program evaluation

std-analytics.name: std-analytics
std-analytics.description: std-analytics — cookieless first-party analytics for one page: on entry it reports a pageview of `path` to the collector at `endpoint`, and each TRACK it hears reports a named event (a download, a sign-up) with its properties. Calls run in the browser through the `analytics` service; an empty `endpoint` or a local host sends nothing. Compose one per tracked page, listed in that page's traits.

std-anim-tick.name: std-anim-tick
std-anim-tick.description: std-anim-tick — sprite animation clock atom. Owns a global animation counter and exposes the current frame NAME (@entity.frameName = frames[counter % len]) every 100ms tick. Boards compose it via `uses` + a trait-ref rebound (linkedEntity) to the board entity; render-ui merges @entity.frameName onto the animated sprite's asset, replacing the inlined animTick frame counters that were duplicated across game boards. 1.1.0 redesign: the 1.0.0 units-frame-advance / effects-aging sets were removed — numeric unit frames served the pre-animation-contract regime (draw-sprite paints atlas sub-texture NAMES, which is exactly what frameName now exposes; zero consumers existed), effects aging is owned by std-fx-particles, and the shared-entity one-writer rule (ORB_SHARED_ENTITY_FIELD_CONFLICT) forbids a shared atom co-writing fields a board's own ticks also write. Tick interval is a language-level literal (100ms); the config surface is `frames`.

std-approval-gate.name: std-approval-gate
std-approval-gate.description: std-approval-gate — generic approval gate / approver workflow. Use when a user voices that an action must be reviewed, approved, signed off, or authorized by a privileged role before it proceeds (admin approval, supervisor sign-off, manager approval, gatekeeper review, editor approval, senior editor approval, reviewer approval, publishing approval, draft approval, content review, submit drafts then editors review and approve or reject, needs approval before going live, requires sign-off before publish). Persists ApprovalRequest rows + surfaces the PENDING ones in a review queue showing what is being approved and who asked, with Approve / Deny actions — Deny captures a written reason. approverRoles is ENFORCED by the review transitions themselves: an APPROVE/DENY from a viewer whose role is not listed does not fire. blockSelfApproval additionally stops a reviewer approving their own request (four-eyes) — DENY stays allowed as self-withdrawal. On approval emits ApprovalGranted; on denial emits ApprovalDenied (with the reason). Hosts that replay the gated action MUST route a failed replay back via APPROVAL_REPLAY_FAILED so the request reopens instead of being silently consumed. Compose onto any orbital whose action you want to gate: the target orbital emits an external event, an ApprovalRequest row is created (stamp subjectLabel/subjectId/requestedBy so reviewers see what they are judging), and downstream effects wait on ApprovalGranted. Differs from std-mod-queue, which is content-moderation-specific.

std-audit-capture.name: std-audit-capture
std-audit-capture.description: std-audit-capture — event-interceptor audit log / audit trail. Use when a user voices that a record's changes must be tracked, logged, or auditable (audit trail, track changes, change history, who edited what, mutation log, record changes, log every edit, edit history, modification log, who did what when, accountability log). Listens for the generic `EntityMutated` sentinel (rename via traitOverrides.events to the real mutation event, e.g. ContactSaved) and persists an AuditEntry row capturing actor, action, entity type/id, before/after snapshots, and timestamp. `captureEventTypes` filters on @payload.data.kind, or on the delivered event's own name when the payload carries no kind (empty = capture all). Every entry also records where the change came from — the delivering event, the behavior and module that emitted it, and the scheduled job when a tick caused it — with no change to the upstream emitter. Compose with `std-lifecycle` to apply retention. Composable via `extraTraits` to interpose audit logging behind any mutating trait.

std-cache-aside.name: std-cache-aside
std-cache-aside.description: infra atom — std-cache-aside (states: cached, empty, error, loading, stale)

std-calendar-sync.name: std-calendar-sync
std-calendar-sync.description: std-calendar-sync — two-way Google Calendar synchronization engine. PUSH: a 15-minute cron scan (and the user-addressable SYNC_NOW) walks `targetEntity` rows whose `externalEventId` marker is blank and creates a remote event per row through calendar.createEvent, reading the summary/start/end via the configured field mapping (`titleField`/`startField`/`endField`/`durationMinutes` fallback/`locationField`/`descriptionField`) — so ANY event-shaped host entity pushes, provided it declares the two marker columns `externalEventId : string` and `syncedAt : number` (the remindedAt precedent). PULL: `CAL_REMOTE_CHANGED` (delivered by the shared /api/hooks/google-calendar ingress from a calendar.watch channel) or the same cycle after a clean push lists remote events (incremental via the in-memory sync token; a restart falls back to a full window list) and upserts each into the atom's own canonical `CalendarEvent` store, matched by `externalEventId` — pulls land in the canonical store, NOT the arbitrary target, because persist keys are static in the language; bind calendar UI to `CalendarEvent` to surface remote events. Conflict detection (local-newer-than-remote) needs a local-modified marker convention and is a recorded gap, not a decorative state. Composes with std-notify-on-event via CAL_SYNCED / CAL_SYNC_FAILED.

std-cascade-on-delete.name: std-cascade-on-delete
std-cascade-on-delete.description: std-cascade-on-delete — relational `owns` cascade. Listens for a parent-deleted sentinel (`ParentDeleted` — rename via traitOverrides.events to the consumer's actual parent-deleted event), then deletes every dependent row whose `foreignKeyField` points at the deleted parent — via a self-driving loop (delete the head of the matching set, re-fetch until none remain). Emits `CascadeRowDeleted` per row and `CascadeCompleted` when done.

std-circuit-breaker.name: std-circuit-breaker
std-circuit-breaker.description: infra atom — std-circuit-breaker (states: closed, halfOpen, open)

std-cooldown.name: std-cooldown
std-cooldown.description: std-cooldown — ability/action cooldown primitive; START begins the countdown, READY fires when it expires.

std-cross-reference.name: std-cross-reference
std-cross-reference.description: std-cross-reference — join-table primitive for N:M relationships. Listens for LinkRequested/UnlinkRequested/FETCH_LINKS_FOR and manages the junction collection (default CrossRefLink [persistent: cross_ref_links]). Rebind via linkedEntity={YourJunction} to your consumer junction; if your junction's id fields differ from leftId/rightId, override them with fields{} renames at the call site. A rebind target must supply leftId, rightId, createdAt, filteredLinks. Emits LinkCreated, LinkRemoved, LinksLoaded as external broadcasts for downstream consumers.

std-data-erasure.name: std-data-erasure
std-data-erasure.description: std-data-erasure — GDPR Art. 17 right-to-be-forgotten queue. Tracks ErasureRequest rows through pending → grace → executed lifecycle with Cancel during grace. v1.0 ships the request lifecycle UI + knob set; auto-emit of ExecuteErasure after grace lands in v1.1 (loop-with-emit gap — docs/Almadar_Std_Factories.md). Target app/ atoms then own the actual delete or piiFields scrub via an ExecuteErasure listener.

std-data-import.name: std-data-import
std-data-import.description: std-data-import — staged CSV import run, source-agnostic: upload → staged review → confirm → parse+map → handoff. UPLOAD_CSV opens a run and persists an ImportBatch row (status uploaded, fieldMappingJson recorded verbatim for provenance); once the batch row is persisted the atom parses the picked file's text with csv/parse and stages it itself with STAGE_ROWS, one JSON string per raw row (a host that parses elsewhere may still answer STAGE_ROWS directly), which the atom bulk-persists into import_rows against the batch id and presents as a staged review (row/error counts + Confirm/Discard). CONFIRM_IMPORT marks the batch confirmed, emits IMPORT_CONFIRMED { batchId, sourceName, rowCount }, and fetches the batch's staged rows; on fetch success the atom parses each rowJson via json/parse, remaps keys through the batch's mappingJson, and emits IMPORT_ROWS_PARSED { batchId, rows, failed } — the persist half is the CONSUMER organism's: it listens for IMPORT_ROWS_PARSED and persists the mapped rows into its own target entity (cross-atom persist into a consumer's entity is not expressible from here). This is deliberately the CSV-file path: the atom never calls a source service — sourceName/fieldMappingJson/targetEntity are consumer configs, and any persist failure marks the batch row failed and fires IMPORT_FAILED, never a silent swallow. Compose with std-import for the file-picker menu.

std-game-clock.name: std-game-clock
std-game-clock.description: std-game-clock — fixed-timestep authoritative clock games compose to drive time; emits GameClockTicked every 100ms while running.

std-global-search.name: std-global-search
std-global-search.description: std-global-search — cross-module federated search. Use when a user voices that one search box should query several modules at once (global search, search everything, unified search, cross-module search, federated search, search across records, omnisearch, one search box, aggregated results, grouped results). One SEARCH event fans out to every module key listed in the `modules` config (comma-separated, deterministic — no registry magic): the trait walks the parsed key list with an internal FAN_OUT_STEP sentinel and emits one scoped MODULE_SEARCH_REQUESTED { moduleKey, queryText, typeFilter, scopeJson } -> external per key, so modules respond in parallel rather than in sequence. Modules answer with SEARCH_RESULTS { moduleKey, resultsJson }; each answer appends a SearchResultGroup to the entity, so the merged view stays grouped by module. A module that answers twice is counted once, a keyless answer is filed under the answering module's name, and every group records which behavior answered it. Client/person/date/type filters ride `scopeJson` — the atom never interprets them. Every query persists as a SearchQuery row (recent/saved searches) when `saveHistory` is on. The input is the mapped `search-input` type rendered inline with event renamed to SEARCH (the std-geosearch idiom); its native {searchTerm}/{value} payloads are bridged via str/default, so programmatic SEARCH { queryText, typeFilter, scopeJson } emitters and the UI box drive the same arm.

std-knowledge-loop.name: std-knowledge-loop
std-knowledge-loop.description: std-knowledge-loop — generic epistemic-loop / decision-gate machinery. Use when a user voices that a claim, hypothesis, or fix needs to be varied, predicted, falsified, independently checked, and calibrated before it is trusted (root-cause investigation, hypothesis testing, a fix that needs sign-off before it ships, a claim that needs a second opinion). The topology (vary -> compare -> hypothesize -> predict -> falsify -> verify -> generalize -> isolate & intervene -> compose -> calibrate -> select next target -> vary again) is fixed and never re-authored per domain. Each gate is announced: entering falsification emits FalsificationRequested, entering verification emits VerificationRequested, entering calibration emits CalibrationRequested (all carry the claim's title + candidateStructure). Who answers a gate is the consumer's call: with manualFalsification / manualVerification on (the default) the atom renders Survived/Failed and Checks-agree/Checks-disagree buttons and a person judges; a consumer that can compute the verdict sets the knob off, authors a sibling trait that listens for the *Requested event, does the domain check, and emits its result, then overrides listens {} at the call site to route that result into SURVIVED/FAILED or CHECKS_AGREE/CHECKS_DISAGREE — the `when` guard on that route IS the consumer's definition of what the gate means (e.g. ReproCheck.REPRO_RESULT -> SURVIVED when (>= ?passRate 0.95)). Calibration is enforced by the atom itself: a submitted numeric score is checked against reliabilityThreshold. On a claim clearing calibration, emits LoopConcluded (title, reliabilityScore) so a composing host can act on the validated result.
std-knowledge-loop.statePattern: calibrating, comparing, composing, falsifying, generalizing, hypothesizing, isolating, predicting, selecting, varying, verifying

std-lifecycle.name: std-lifecycle
std-lifecycle.description: std-lifecycle — age-based status lifecycle for a target entity. A periodic tick scans the target for records in `fromStatus` whose `dateField` is older than `ageDays`, and transitions each one to `toStatus` — every matching record, via a self-driving scan loop (process the head of a filtered fetch, persist the status, re-fetch until the set drains). Compose onto any orbital and bind `targetEntity` + the status/date knobs.

std-migration-job.name: std-migration-job
std-migration-job.description: std-migration-job — one import run of external data into the host system, modeled as a persistent MigrationJob row with a lifecycle state machine: idle → fetching → mapping → reviewing → committing → done | failed. All source access goes through the migration service (call-service "migration" listDocuments / fetchDocument / commit) — the atom never talks to a source directly, and the host-injected service handler resolves credentials from the connectionRef knob (a reference, never the secret). Once documents are listed the atom asks the migration service to stage them (call-service "migration" stage — the source's stored profile replayed with no commit), whose result arrives as MIGRATION_STAGED with stats and the staged units/skipped/validationErrors rows; a host that stages through an agent may send MIGRATION_STAGED itself — when the rows are supplied, reviewing renders an ImportPreviewTree so the user can see what will commit before approving. The user approves (MIGRATION_APPROVED) and only then does commit run. Terminal runs persist the job row for provenance. Rebind the entity to a host-owned job entity via linkedEntity; target, connectionRef and reviewSlot are config knobs.
std-migration-job.statePattern: committing, done, failed, fetching, idle, mapping, reviewing

std-mod-queue.name: std-mod-queue
std-mod-queue.description: std-mod-queue — moderation queue for content review. Owns a ModQueueItem entity (one row per flagged target) and a single review trait that loads pending items, renders them in a data-grid with Approve / Reject / Escalate actions, and persists the reviewer's verdict back to the row.

std-notification-center.name: std-notification-center
std-notification-center.description: std-notification-center — per-user notification preferences, web-push subscriptions, and the digest drain for suppressed notifications. Owns the two owner-scoped stores std-notify-on-event consults at dispatch time: NotificationPreference rows (per event key: mode instant/digest/off, channel override, per-user quiet hours) and PushSubscription rows (captured via the browser/push-subscribe flow — the shared service worker + PushManager subscription, persisted as flat endpoint/p256dh/auth credentials). The DigestDrain trait is the delivery half of every suppression std-notify-on-event records: an hourly cron tick scans NotificationRecord audit rows left undispatched for digest/quiet-hours reasons and at least `minAgeHours` old, delivers each by email (the digest channel), and marks it dispatched — the reminder-scheduler self-driving scan loop verbatim. Compose alongside std-notify-on-event: the listener suppresses and records, this atom captures subscriptions, edits preferences, and drains.

std-notification-preferences.name: std-notification-preferences
std-notification-preferences.description: std-notification-preferences — per-person notification preference store plus a consultable gate. Owns NotificationPreference rows (one per person + event key: channel override in_app/email/push/slack/sms/webhook, mode instant/digest/off, quiet-hours window 'HH:MM-HH:MM' such as 22:00-07:00). The PreferencesManage trait is standard CRUD over the store (list / create / update / delete, persisted, success/failure cascade arms): a data-grid browse plus ModalRecordModal create/edit forms whose SAVE carries the full row payload (std-list daisy-chain idiom). The PreferenceGate trait is the consult half other notify traits call: emit CHECK_PREFERENCE { personId, eventKey } and the gate fetches the matching row (a row whose eventKey is blank applies to every event) and answers PREFERENCE_RESOLVED { personId, eventKey, channel, mode, suppressed } — suppressed is true only when the row's quietHours window covers the current hour; mode 'digest' rides on the verdict for the caller to defer. Default policy: no matching row — or a failed lookup — resolves fail-open to { channel: in_app, mode: instant, suppressed: false }; the absence of a preference never silences a notification.

std-notify-on-event.name: std-notify-on-event
std-notify-on-event.description: std-notify-on-event — cross-orbital wiring atom. Subscribes to events from another orbital (e.g. CheckoutOrbital emits OrderPlaced, OrderRecordOrbital reacts via this atom) and dispatches a notification. Use when one orbital needs to react to or be notified about events that happen in another orbital — the wiring goes through this atom's `EventOccurred` listener which the molecule renames via traitOverrides.events to the upstream event name. Dispatch gates on `guardOp`: `eq` (default) does string-equality on `triggerStatus` against the upstream event's `status` field; `gt`/`lt`/`gte`/`lte` instead numerically compare `guardField` (read from the event's `data` payload) against `guardValue`, for threshold-crossing asks such as low-stock alerts. Resolves recipient from `recipients` (first entry; multi-recipient fan-out is a future extension), falling back to `fallbackRecipient` when set, or `@user.id` otherwise. Skips dispatch when the recipient is in `suppressionList`. Delivery consults std-notification-center data before dispatching: per-person NotificationPreference rows (matched on `personId` = recipient and `eventKey` = this listener's `eventKey`, blank = all) can mute (`mode: off`), defer to the digest drain (`mode: digest`), override the channel, or impose per-user quiet hours (a 'HH:MM-HH:MM' window, blank = none); the atom-level `quietStartHour`/`quietEndHour` window and the `frequencyCapPerWeek` rolling cap (counted against dispatched NotificationRecord audit rows for the same recipient + channel) suppress likewise. Every suppression persists an honest audit row (`dispatched: false` with the reason in `error`: quiet-hours / digest-deferred / muted-by-preference / frequency-cap / no-push-subscription) which std-notification-center's digest cycle drains later. Channels: `in-app` emits the `notify` toast; `email`/`sms`/`webhook` dispatch through call-service (email.send / twilio.sendSMS / webhook.send); `push` looks up the recipient's PushSubscription row (owned by std-notification-center) and dispatches web-push via push.send (`pushTitle` falls back to `template`; `pushDeepLink`/`pushIcon` optional). The audit row's `dispatched` flag is honest — true only once the service call succeeds.

std-page-open.name: std-page-open
std-page-open.description: std-page-open — opens a URL in a new, focused browser tab and reports the tab. Wire OPEN to something the person does (a button or a row action), so a page only ever opens because they asked for it. Needs a host with the `page` service (a browser extension).

std-page-search.name: std-page-search
std-page-search.description: std-page-search — runs one search on a site in a background tab: opens `searchUrl` with the query as the `queryParam` parameter, reads up to `maxResults` elements matching `resultSelector` (waiting up to `waitMs` for the results to appear), closes the tab, and reports RESULTS with the fields read from each. One search at a time: SEARCH is accepted again once RESULTS or SEARCH_FAILED is reported. It never clicks anything. Needs a host with the `page` service (a browser extension with access to the search pages).

std-page-treat.name: std-page-treat
std-page-treat.description: std-page-treat — applies a declared visual treatment to one element of a browser tab (hide, blur, highlight, or label it with text) or restores it, and reports which element it treated. TREAT takes the tab and element id std-page-watch reports; TREAT_MANY treats a whole list at once and reports which elements were treated and which had already left their page. The treatments are a fixed, declared set: no arbitrary styles or scripts. Needs a host with the `page` service (a browser extension).

std-page-watch.name: std-page-watch
std-page-watch.description: std-page-watch — watches every browser tab whose URL matches `match` for elements matching `itemSelector`, and reports each element once as ITEM with the `fields` read from it, now and as the page changes. Needs a host with the `page` service (a browser extension, which asks for access to exactly the `match` pages). Each item carries its tab and element id; compose std-page-treat to hide, blur, highlight or label it.

std-permission-matrix.name: std-permission-matrix
std-permission-matrix.description: std-permission-matrix — role × module permission grant table / capability matrix admin surface. Use when a user voices that permissions must be managed per role and module (permission matrix, role permissions, capability matrix, permission grants, access matrix, who can see finance, hide margins, module-level permissions, admin permission screen, grant management, finance visibility by role, restrict modules by role). Persists PermissionGrant rows (workspaceId + role + module + capability flags canReadFinance / canSeeOthersHours / canSeeMargins) with full CRUD on an admin page mounted at /admin/permissions — create/edit forms are the std-modal ModalRecordModal substrate (the corpus's two-trait CRUD shape, mirroring std-list), persists live in a sibling coordinator trait, and adminRoles is ENFORCED at the persist boundary (a viewer whose role is not listed cannot fire a write, from the button or from the bus). Ships a query trait other traits consult event-wise: CHECK_GRANT { role, module } fetches the matching grant(s) and re-emits GRANT_RESOLVED { role, module, canReadFinance, canSeeOthersHours, canSeeMargins, found }. Grant SURFACE only — entity-layer @read/@update gate integration is a recorded core gap (gates are pure @entity/@user S-expressions and cannot consult another entity's rows), so enforcement stays with the consumer until that core lands.

std-record-store.name: std-record-store
std-record-store.description: std-record-store — saves the records other traits collect. Route a form's SAVE to DO_CREATE or DO_UPDATE and a delete confirmation to DO_DELETE; it runs the persist and emits RECORD_CREATED / RECORD_UPDATED / RECORD_DELETED so lists can reload.

std-reminder-scheduler.name: std-reminder-scheduler
std-reminder-scheduler.description: std-reminder-scheduler — deadline reminders for a target entity. A periodic tick scans the target for records whose `dateField` deadline (a ms-epoch number or an ISO datetime string) is within `offsetHours` of now and that have not been reminded yet, and emits `ReminderDue` for each — every matching record, via a self-driving scan loop. `direction` picks which side of now the scan matches: 'future' (default) fires for deadlines up to `offsetHours` ahead; 'past' fires once a record's date is at least `offsetHours` behind now. Marks each record `remindedAt` so it isn't reminded twice — and only when the record actually matched the scan, so records outside the window stay eligible for later passes. Compose alongside std-notify-on-event to deliver the reminder.

std-review-cycle.name: std-review-cycle
std-review-cycle.description: std-review-cycle — revise-and-resubmit review workflow (document review, pull-request review, design review, editorial review, submission review, send back for changes, request changes, resubmit, review rounds, four-eyes approval). A record moves draft → in review → changes requested → in review → … → approved. One SUBMIT event serves both the first submission and every resubmission; the atom counts review rounds and marks resubmissions on the emitted ReviewRequested. Every move writes a ReviewEvent history row stamped with the states it left and entered. `requireSeparateApproval` enforces four-eyes review: an approval raised in the same action that submitted the record (an auto-responding rule or bot) is rejected. Headless — the host renders the badge and buttons and routes its actions to SUBMIT / REQUEST_CHANGES / APPROVE.

std-row-access-control.name: std-row-access-control
std-row-access-control.description: std-row-access-control — row-level access control gate / ownership filter / role-based row visibility. Use when a user voices that only certain users should see or edit certain records (only the owner can edit, private to owner, owner-only visibility, only see your own records, role-based visibility, admin-only access, visible to admins only, restricted to role, permission gate, ownership scoping, hide from other users, only show mine). Listens for `RowsLoaded` (rename via traitOverrides.events to the consumer's load event), filters `@payload.data` by `@user.id` (when `ownerField` is set) and/or `@user.role` (when `visibleRoles` is non-empty), re-emits `RowsFiltered` for downstream consumers (rename to wire into the UI atom's listen). Composable via `extraTraits` to interpose between a data fetch and a list/grid UI.

std-status-lifecycle.name: std-status-lifecycle
std-status-lifecycle.description: Infra substrate: data-driven entity status lifecycle. The statuses and the allowed transitions are config data over a fixed single-state topology, so a host organism can expand or collapse its lifecycle without forking. Compose onto an entity, rename the ChangeStatusRequested listen to the host's status-change action, and supply `states` + `transitions`. A requested move is validated against the `transitions` table (illegal moves are rejected), then the new value is written to `statusField` on the target entity and StatusChanged is emitted. Surfaces nothing — the host renders the badge and buttons.

std-status-lifecycle-control.name: std-status-lifecycle-control
std-status-lifecycle-control.description: Status lifecycle control — infra molecule pairing std-status-lifecycle's StatusMachine, which deliberately surfaces no UI of its own. Pure presentational: shows the current status and one button per legal next move (config.transitions filtered on config.currentStatus), emitting ChangeStatusRequested with the picked move's id/from/to on click. Driven entirely by config (currentStatus/recordId/transitions) rather than a bound entity, so a host embeds it inline at the record it's viewing (currentStatus={@entity.status} recordId={@entity.id} transitions matching the paired StatusMachine's own config.transitions) and points that StatusMachine's `listens` at this trait's emit (`<Composer>.ChangeStatusRequested -> ChangeStatusRequested`) instead of at a dead declared-only event.

std-data-collector.name: std-data-collector
std-data-collector.description: std-data-collector — pure buffer-accumulation atom, parameterized for any ML domain. Collects data points into a buffer and fires BUFFER_READY with the full accumulated buffer once it reaches config.bufferSize, then resets for the next cycle. No ML compute, no model call — state machine + array operators only. Use ahead of a training loop, a batch inference call, or any downstream rung that needs a fixed-size window of accumulated observations.

std-graph-builder.name: std-graph-builder
std-graph-builder.description: Graph construction atom — builds node/edge structures from an entity collection for downstream GNN pipelines; pure array/object transform, no ML compute.

std-ml-classify.name: std-ml-classify
std-ml-classify.description: Generative rung (R5) — structured LLM verdict from a closed category set, via the llm.classify service seam. Bottom of the fall-through: always answers or fails, never abstains.

std-ml-exact-check.name: std-ml-exact-check
std-ml-exact-check.description: Rung R0 of the intelligence ladder — normalizes and compares a candidate value against a key value; abstains on no match.

std-ml-infer.name: std-ml-infer
std-ml-infer.description: std-ml-infer — the learned rung (R4) of the intelligence ladder, and the seam between a .lolo circuit and a trained model deployed on masar (or off-the-shelf HuggingFace weights) reached through the ml service. Sends the caller-supplied input straight to call-service ml infer, then guards the raw output before it ever becomes an effect: validates it against the declared outputContract, clamps it into range, and only then decides. Emits INFERRED when the output satisfies the contract and confidence clears confidenceFloor — carrying the clamped output, confidence, and an empty violations list. Otherwise abstains with INFER_ABSTAINED, whose reason is one of: low confidence (contract satisfied but below floor, violations empty), contract violation (violations populated via contract/violations for diagnosis), or unavailable (the service call itself failed — a masar cold start or a down endpoint, never surfaced as a user-visible error). Use when a numeric or tensor-shaped model answer needs a licensed guard before becoming a decision — classification scores, regressions, embedding-derived predictions — and the next rung (R5 generative) should take over on any abstain.

std-ml-label-capture.name: std-ml-label-capture
std-ml-label-capture.description: std-ml-label-capture — records a labeled example (input, verdict, source rung, observed outcome) so that expensive top-rung answers become training data for a cheaper rung later. Generic: it knows nothing about grading or students. sampleRate gates what fraction of examples are kept (1 = capture all); sink tags which named destination the example is attributed to.

std-ml-lookup.name: std-ml-lookup
std-ml-lookup.description: Rung R1 of the intelligence ladder — finds the candidate value in a list of accepted values; abstains when nothing matches.

std-ml-posterior.name: std-ml-posterior
std-ml-posterior.description: std-ml-posterior — the statistical rung (R2) of the intelligence ladder. Holds a Beta(alpha, beta) belief over an unknown success rate and updates it from boolean observations (Bayesian updating, knowledge tracing, Thompson-sampling prior). After each observation it draws samples from the posterior, computes a credible interval, and decides: MASTERY_REACHED when the mean clears the floor with a tight interval, REMEDIATION_NEEDED when the mean sits at or below the ceiling with the same confidence, or EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT — the abstain — when the interval is still too wide to trust. Use when a hand-tuned score needs to become a belief that can say 'not enough evidence yet' (mastery, skill, risk, preference, difficulty).

std-ml-similarity.name: std-ml-similarity
std-ml-similarity.description: Retrieval rung (R3) — embed a candidate against references and gate on cosine floor + margin; abstains when not confident.

std-tokenizer.name: std-tokenizer
std-tokenizer.description: std-tokenizer — a text-preprocessing atom for tokenization. Splits raw text into a token sequence using a configurable method (whitespace, character, or arbitrary delimiter), normalizes and truncates the sequence, then maps each token to a vocabulary id (falling back to unkId when the token is absent from config.vocab). Feeds downstream embedding or sequence-model atoms. Pure circuit logic: str/* and array/* operators only, no ML compute, no model call.

std-weight-validator.name: std-weight-validator
std-weight-validator.description: std-weight-validator — a constraint-checking atom for model weights, applying the same discipline as the zero-warning validator to weights: constrained and checked, not trusted (Almadar_Intelligence_Ladder.md §7.5). Checks a candidate weight tensor against three pure predicate constraints — magnitude bounds (every element's absolute value must clear maxMagnitude), forbidden regions (excluded [min,max] bands no weight may land in even within the magnitude bound), and a regression threshold against a baseline tensor (per-element drift must not exceed regressionThreshold; 0 disables the check) — and reports every violated check with its detail. Emits WEIGHTS_ACCEPTED when all three checks clear, or WEIGHTS_REJECTED carrying the full violations list otherwise. Pure circuit logic: predicates and comparisons only, no ML compute, no model call.

std-escalating-decision.name: std-escalating-decision
std-escalating-decision.description: std-escalating-decision — the intelligence ladder itself, as one reusable composition. One request enters at DECIDE and falls through the rungs in order — R0 exact check, R1 table lookup, R3 retrieval, R4 learned inference, R5 generative classification — each rung handing off to the next by abstaining, until one proves the answer. Exits DECIDED, tagged with which rung answered (rung, confidence, matched, reasoning), or DECISION_FAILED if even the generative floor could not serve it. The escalation is a chain, not a hub: each rung listens directly to the rung above it and projects its own inputs out of the carried request, so the trait graph is a DAG and no event ever returns to a rung that already ran. Domain-agnostic: it knows about candidates and categories, not students or quizzes — grading, routing, matching, moderation, and duplicate detection are all this same molecule with different knobs. R2 (the Beta posterior) is deliberately not in this chain: it is the 'decide what to do next' half of a turn and already lives in std-knowledge-tracing.

std-knowledge-tracing.name: std-knowledge-tracing
std-knowledge-tracing.description: std-knowledge-tracing — turns one true/false observation ('did the learner get this right?') into a tracked belief about mastery, and captures the same observation as a labeled training example in the same motion. Composes std-ml-posterior (the R2 statistical rung — a Beta-Bernoulli belief over an unknown success rate) with std-ml-label-capture: every posterior verdict — MASTERY_REACHED, REMEDIATION_NEEDED, or the abstain EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT — becomes a persisted labeled example (the input skill, the posterior's own verdict, and the ground-truth outcome that produced it), so a cheaper rung can later be trained to reproduce the same call without running the statistics. Domain-agnostic: it knows about skills and observations, not students, quizzes, or courses. One instance tracks one belief (e.g. one learner × one skill); the host composes as many instances as it has beliefs to hold.

std-avl-cosmic-zoom.name: std-avl-cosmic-zoom
std-avl-cosmic-zoom.description: std-avl-cosmic-zoom — a whole app, drillable: the system map (one chip per orbital and the event wires between them, with a Dependencies lens over what each orbital imports), then one orbital's traits as state machines, then one transition as circuits. Step plays the transition on the kernel (`program/step`) and lights the machines and circuits with the run; a scene slider replays earlier steps. LOAD hands it the program to show (resolved) and the program as written (for its imports). Use for code workspaces and editors that let people explore how an app is wired.
std-avl-cosmic-zoom.capabilities: explore an app's orbitals and wires, drill into an orbital's state machines, play a transition step by step, see what an app imports

ui-avl-glyph.name: ui-avl-glyph
ui-avl-glyph.description: AvlGlyph — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui avl-glyph pattern).

ui-avl-state-machine.name: ui-avl-state-machine
ui-avl-state-machine.description: AvlStateMachine — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui avl-state-machine pattern).

ui-avl-transition-detail.name: ui-avl-transition-detail
ui-avl-transition-detail.description: One transition explained: from-state, event and to-state, the guard that must hold, and each effect it runs in order, drawn as circuit boards. — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui avl-transition-detail pattern).
ui-avl-transition-detail.capabilities: transition explainer, event guard effects walkthrough, state machine step detail

ui-avl-transition-explainer.name: ui-avl-transition-explainer
ui-avl-transition-explainer.description: One transition explained step by step: from-state, event and to-state, the guard that must hold, and each effect it runs in order. — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui avl-transition-explainer pattern).
ui-avl-transition-explainer.capabilities: transition explainer, event guard effects walkthrough, what happens when an event fires

ui-behavior-view.name: ui-behavior-view
ui-behavior-view.description: BehaviorView — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui behavior-view pattern).

ui-module-card.name: ui-module-card
ui-module-card.description: ModuleCard — a compact summary card for one orbital module: its entity and fields, a mini state machine per trait, and its pages. — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui module-card pattern).
ui-module-card.capabilities: orbital module summary card, entity and trait overview card, app architecture node card

ui-flow-canvas.name: ui-flow-canvas
ui-flow-canvas.description: FlowCanvas — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui flow-canvas pattern).

ui-layers-panel.name: ui-layers-panel
ui-layers-panel.description: LayersPanel — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui layers-panel pattern).

ui-orb-inspector.name: ui-orb-inspector
ui-orb-inspector.description: OrbInspector — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui orb-inspector pattern).

std-app-layout.name: std-app-layout
std-app-layout.description: std-app-layout — dashboard-layout chrome (sidebar nav + top bar with search + topBarActions + notifications) wrapping a single contentTrait slot. Use for list-style apps (CMS / helpdesk / CRM) and account/settings pages: the chrome stays stable while the consumer's content trait renders the data, and the consumer can add domain icons (cart / profile / help) via topBarActions. Bind once per orbital — the consumer rebinds linkedEntity via `XAppLayout = AppShell.traits.AppLayout -> XEntity` so multiple orbitals in one file each get their own chrome without colliding on a shared atom entity.
std-app-layout.capabilities: settings page shell, preferences page, account settings layout, profile settings, admin console shell

std-app-search.name: std-app-search
std-app-search.description: std-app-search — reusable global search: wraps a host content view and, on a SEARCH trigger, fetches the linked entity filtered by @config.searchField and renders the matching results, then CLEAR_SEARCH returns to the host view. Rebind to any entity; point @config.idleContent at the normal view and wire a trigger (e.g. AppLayout SEARCH) into SEARCH.

std-behavior-catalog.name: std-behavior-catalog
std-behavior-catalog.description: std-behavior-catalog — browse the installed behaviors under the `scope` registry folders (`behavior/catalog`), search them by meaning (the query is embedded with `call-service llm embed` and ranked by cosine similarity to each behavior's description; results under `minScore` drop out), open one's knobs and events (`behavior/describe`), and pick one: PICKED { behavior, trait, value } carries the behavior name, its first trait as a value ready to bind, and the whole behavior as a value ready to embed or store. With `pick: toggle` each card carries an on/off switch instead: TOGGLED { behavior, checked, topic, value } per change, and SELECTION { behaviors } seeds which are on. Pick for block libraries, plugin pickers, plugin on/off settings and any page that lets users choose a building block.
std-behavior-catalog.capabilities: browse installed behaviors, search behaviors by meaning, describe a behavior's knobs and events, pick a behavior to bind

std-behavior-tour.name: std-behavior-tour
std-behavior-tour.description: std-behavior-tour — plays a real behavior through a scripted sequence so people can watch it work: a guided demo on a website, or a step-by-step tutorial. The composing program embeds the running behavior in the `demo` slot and lists `events` (the event each step sends) and `captions` (what is shown while it plays; only ever rendered, so they may be translated). The composed std-learn-transport owns Play / Pause / Step / Reset and the clock; on every step the tour emits TOUR_STEP { index, event } and shows that step's caption, and the program routes TOUR_STEP to the behavior's own events with a filtered listen (`Tour.TOUR_STEP -> MOVE when (= ?event "MOVE")`). Reset emits TOUR_RESET. `loop` quietly resets the demo after the last step (TOUR_RESET, intro caption) and plays again. `playWhenVisible` starts it the first time it scrolls into view (never under reduced motion), and `compact` keeps only Play / Pause and Reset, and `demoTheme` shows the demo in its own theme so it stands apart from the page. Pick to demonstrate or teach a behavior.

std-billable-hour.name: std-billable-hour
std-billable-hour.description: std-billable-hour — generic billable-hour timesheet primitive for legal, agency, and consulting domains. Lists entries in `browsing`; opens entry detail in `viewing_single` with Invoice / Write Off actions.

std-board.name: std-board
std-board.description: std-board — generic N-column board primitive. `config.columns` is an array of column definitions ({ key, label, icon, variant }); the trait `array/map`s them on `BoardItemsLoaded` into `@entity.boards` where each board carries its filtered items + a count. The render is a `data-grid` over `@entity.boards` (one card per column) whose `renderItem` lambda nests a `data-list` over `@col.items` (the cards in that stage). N is config-driven — pass any number of columns; the outer `data-grid`'s `cols` is bound to `@config.gridCols` so the grid wraps if you exceed it. Topology = loading / viewing_board / viewing_card / adding / error — distinct from the cookie-cutter `loading/browsing/viewing_single/error` CRUD shape. App-level atoms (e.g. std-pipeline) compose std-board via `uses` and add a sibling persistor + extended source entity. `config.boardLook` switches the board body between the default N-column grid ('columns') and a Trello-style wide-column kanban ('kanban-classic'). `viewing_board` listens for REFETCH_QUERY/REFETCH_FILTER/REFETCH_PAGE (the std-search/std-filter/std-pagination wiring targets, no render on refetch — @entity.boards is bound reactively) and can optionally render its own search box (config.bodySearch, default false) and filter bar (config.filters, default []); no pagination control is rendered — a board's columns are not a paged list.

std-book-reader.name: std-book-reader
std-book-reader.description: std-book-reader — reads a multi-chapter book one chapter at a time. Opens on a cover (cover image, title, subtitle, author, a start button and the table of contents); reading shows a contents rail with the current chapter marked, the chapter title and progress, the chapter text (markdown) and previous/next buttons. Supports right-to-left books. Emits CHAPTER_OPENED on every chapter change. Pick for handbooks, manifestos, course readers and long-form guides.

std-browse.name: std-browse
std-browse.description: std-browse as a Function — single primitive: data-grid. Owns the fetch + REFETCH (query/filter/page) state machine. Consumers configure fields/imageField/itemActions/cols/gap/variant; the atom renders the grid. Each `fields[]` entry accepts `{ name, label, variant }` plus optional `referenceEntity` + `displayField` to render a foreign-key column as the joined entity's display value (data-grid resolves @list[referenceEntity] at render time when both keys are present). `browseLook` (table default / dense / feed / gallery / master-detail / triage) selects one of six render bodies; dense/feed/gallery were folded in from std-browse-dense/-feed/-gallery (Phase 5.B); master-detail (split record view driven by the guarded VIEW/CLOSE self-transitions) and triage (inbox rows) were folded in 2026-07-26. Consumers retarget by setting browseLook.

std-calendar.name: std-calendar
std-calendar.description: std-calendar as a Function — owns the fetch + SELECT_DAY state machine; default bodyContent renders the month-grid + upcoming-events tree. `config.calendarLook` switches the body between the default month-grid ('month'), a day-grouped agenda list ('agenda-list'), and a 7-column week timeline ('week-timeline') while inheriting the same trait, state machine, emits, and listens.

std-card-grid.name: std-card-grid
std-card-grid.description: std-card-grid — a titled grid of content cards from a config list. Each card can carry an image (screenshots, portfolio, case studies), a portrait (team members), an icon, a badge, a title, a description and a link. `look` picks media cards, centered profile cards, or plain text cards. Pick for showcases, team pages, case studies, service catalogs and testimonials.

std-confirmation.name: std-confirmation
std-confirmation.description: Modal-only confirmation trait: renders ONLY to the `modal` slot. Consumers configure icon/title/alertMessage/confirmLabel at the trait-ref call site via `config: { ... }`. Side effects (persist delete, notify, etc.) belong in a sibling coordinator trait that `listens { ConfirmTrait CONFIRM -> DO_DELETE }`.

std-dashboard-grid-embedded.name: std-dashboard-grid-embedded
std-dashboard-grid-embedded.description: std-dashboard-grid-embedded — embeddable sibling of std-dashboard-grid-layout. Renders the same toolbar / filter / 12-tile grid contract WITHOUT wrapping it in dashboard-layout chrome (no sidebar, no appName, no nav). Use inside another app shell that already owns the surrounding chrome.

std-date-range.name: std-date-range
std-date-range.description: std-date-range — compact calendar button (Looker / Tableau shape) that opens a popover containing the date-range-picker. Owns a DateRange runtime entity; DATE_RANGE_CHANGED persists @payload.from + @payload.to so cross-trait listeners can route the range into data atoms (Browse REFETCH_FILTER, Stats / Graphs requery).

std-detail-layout.name: std-detail-layout
std-detail-layout.description: std-detail-layout — detail-page chrome band (back button + navigation-stack breadcrumb trail) above a single contentTrait slot. Use as the contentTrait of a detail page's AppShell binding: the band renders `Contracts › Contract details` (phones: `← Back`) from the orbital-scoped client navigation stack (session history, seeded from declared page-path ancestry on cold loads — the trail is never empty), and the consumer's detail trait renders below it. Back pops the stack; crumb clicks navigate to their level; a list router's `(navigate path payload { crumb: ?row.title })` labels the detail crumb with the real record title. Bind once per detail page — `XDetailLayout = DetailShell.traits.DetailLayout` with `contentTrait: @trait.XDetail`.
std-detail-layout.capabilities: detail page shell, breadcrumb trail, back navigation, record detail chrome, navigation stack, drill-down hierarchy

std-doc-page.name: std-doc-page
std-doc-page.description: std-doc-page — one page of a documentation site: a section sidebar with the current page marked, a breadcrumb, the page title and lede, an "on this page" contents list, the page's own content (a render slot the call site fills, live behaviors included) and previous/next links. Supports right-to-left pages. Pick for docs sites, handbooks, reference manuals and knowledge bases.

std-esign-flow.name: std-esign-flow
std-esign-flow.description: std-esign-flow — the send-for-signature flow: list signature requests, create one (pick document + recipient), resend or cancel, track status. Composes std-file-store + std-esign-request; no document-rendering or code-preview chrome. v1.2 (W5): EnvelopeDispatcher wires sessions to the real `esign` service — SEND_ENVELOPE dispatches a DocuSign envelope (the document rides the event as an UploadDropZone-shaped file payload, since StoredFile rows are metadata-only) and stamps `envelopeId`/`sentAt`/status=sent; the browse grid's per-row "Refresh status" pulls getEnvelopeStatus and maps completed/delivered/declined onto signed/viewed/declined.

std-esign-request.name: std-esign-request
std-esign-request.description: std-esign-request — specialized e-signature request tracker: send a document out for signing and track its status (draft/sent/viewed/signed/declined/expired). Just the request list + send/revoke; signature capture is std-signature-capture's job.

std-event-log.name: std-event-log
std-event-log.description: std-event-log — generic chronological event feed (Stripe activity log / GitHub PR timeline / Linear event feed style). Renders a vertical `timeline` with type-coded dots, a single horizontal chip-bar of kind filters (All + per-kind), reverse-chronological sort, and an inline form for logging events that weren't auto-captured. `config.kindOptions` maps each kind → status/icon/label so consuming molecules/organisms get type-coded visuals without re-implementing topology. Topology = loading / viewing / backfilling / error.

std-export.name: std-export
std-export.description: std-export — a dropdown format menu (CSV/XLSX/PDF defaults; caller can override via config.formats). Emits EXPORT_REQUESTED { itemId, label } on the bus — itemId is the picked format id; host or sibling orbital generates the file. A format entry may carry `url`: the menu then downloads that file directly on pick (gesture-driven; the event still emits) — used for pre-baked artifacts like sprite sheets. tileId is a static per-instance config value, not echoed in the click payload.

std-file-store.name: std-file-store
std-file-store.description: std-file-store — the generic file/page tree primitive. A file-tree + config-driven data table over a hierarchical collection; opens a row in `viewing_single` with config-driven detail actions. Rebindable: pass `fields`/`itemActions`/`detailActions`/`tree` to retarget it at any hierarchical entity (files, wiki pages, note trees). Folds in the former std-page-tree via `reorderable` + a page field/action set.

std-filter.name: std-filter
std-filter.description: std-filter — single primitive: filter-group. Owns a FilterTarget runtime entity; every FILTER transition persists field/value so cross-trait listeners can route the latest selection into data atoms.

std-form-advanced.name: std-form-advanced
std-form-advanced.description: std-form-advanced — full-typed form-section primitive. Hosts the `editing` state with a configurable `fields` array (each entry mirrors @almadar/ui's `form-section` field schema: `{ name, label, type?, values?, relation?, required? }`). Agents drive shape by overriding `config.fields` per-call-site.

std-gallery.name: std-gallery
std-gallery.description: std-gallery — image gallery primitive. Browses GalleryItems in a media-gallery grid; opens a lightbox modal for full-size viewing.

std-gantt-schedule.name: std-gantt-schedule
std-gantt-schedule.description: std-gantt-schedule — GENERIC view-only Gantt/timeline atom: fetches a task collection on INIT and renders it as bars on a day-scale axis via the gantt pattern, with group headers, dependency arrows, and a today marker. Fully rebindable: a host overrides the linked entity and points the field-mapping configs (labelField/startField/endField/durationField/statusField/groupField) at its own columns; clicking a bar emits the config-named onBarClick event with the row id. No drag-edit, no zoom — schedule viewing only.

std-geosearch.name: std-geosearch
std-geosearch.description: std-geosearch — location-aware search variant: search-input + map-view + range-slider for radius. Owns a GeoSearchResult runtime entity; GEO_SEARCH persists @payload.searchTerm/lat/lng/radiusKm so cross-trait listeners can route them into geo-aware data atoms.

std-graphs.name: std-graphs
std-graphs.description: std-graphs — embeddable chart atom. ITEMS_LOADED keeps the rows whose @config.filterField equals @config.filterValue (blank = all), groups them by @config.categoryField, or (timeAxis=true) by the @config.period bucket of @config.timeField — rows without a time value (or, by category, without a category value) have no bucket to land in and are left out — and aggregates per bucket. Multi-series rendering via @config.series (preformatted ChartSeries shape). Histograms via chartType=histogram pass pre-binned @payload.data through unchanged. Stacked / 100% stacked bars via @config.stack. Post-process sort + limit. Clicking a data point emits UI:@config.drillEvent with { label, value, seriesLabel? }. Drop into a dashboard alongside std-stats / std-browse.

std-hero.name: std-hero
std-hero.description: std-hero — the headline block at the top of a page, or a call-to-action banner further down. Optional eyebrow badge, headline, supporting text, up to two link actions, an optional copyable command, optional media below or beside the copy, and an optional backdrop scene behind it all. `look: banner` turns it into a contained call-to-action card. Links follow `href` (in-app path, #anchor, or absolute URL); each click also emits CTA_PRIMARY / CTA_SECONDARY with the href. Pick for landing, product, pricing and campaign pages.

std-home.name: std-home
std-home.description: std-home — the home page of an app: a welcome header, then an actionable overview gathered from the app's other pages. `homeLook` picks one of five layouts. Every look puts the headline figures directly under the greeting. For staff running the business: command (then actions, sections and shortcut tiles), briefing (then sections in the main column with actions and shortcut links in a side rail), launchpad (then big shortcut tiles before the sections). For customers: spotlight (a photo or gradient hero with a curved edge, then actions, shortcut tiles and their own items) and concierge (a centred greeting, then a grid of shortcut tiles and their items). Everything is actionable: `shortcuts` are links to other pages, `actions` are the organism's own operation triggers (open a create form, start a flow), and `sections` are lists whose rows act. When there are no sections yet the page shows an empty state that still offers every shortcut. Pick as the first page of any back office or customer experience.

std-image-upload-multi.name: std-image-upload-multi
std-image-upload-multi.description: std-image-upload-multi — multi-image upload with drop zone, gallery preview, and per-batch progress.

std-import.name: std-import
std-import.description: std-import — a dropdown source menu (Paste text / Markdown files defaults; caller can override via config.sources) plus the OS file picker for file-kind sources. Emits IMPORT_REQUESTED { source, files } on the bus — source is the picked SourceOption descriptor; files carries file metadata when the picker ran (empty otherwise). The actual import work is delegated to a sibling std-migration-job, which listens for IMPORT_REQUESTED and drives the migration service. Mirrors std-export: the menu emits each entry's own literal event field, so overriding the event alone does not retarget the click — also set sources[].event to match.

std-language-picker.name: std-language-picker
std-language-picker.description: std-language-picker — the language switcher of a multilingual site or app: a globe button showing the current language code that opens a menu listing every language in its own name, with the current one ticked. Each entry links to the same page in that language. Routing convention: the default language lives at the root and every other language under a `/<code>/` prefix (`/pricing`, `/ar/pricing`, `/sl/pricing`), so each language has its own stable URL that can be linked from outside and indexed by search engines. Pick for public websites and app chrome that serve more than one language; std-site-header embeds it.

std-media-section.name: std-media-section
std-media-section.description: std-media-section — content rows that pair copy with a screenshot or illustration: each row has an eyebrow, heading, body text, a short bullet list and an optional link action on one side and its media on the other, and consecutive rows alternate sides. A row without media sits alone at reading width. Stacks on small screens. Pick for 'how it works', product tours and feature-detail pages.

std-modal-editor.name: std-modal-editor
std-modal-editor.description: UI substrate: modal keyboard editing over any editable CodeBlock. The topology is fixed (NORMAL / INSERT / VISUAL / OPERATOR_PENDING / COMMAND) and every binding is config: mode-entry keys, motions, operators, ex-commands, the digit table that accumulates a repeat count, and the per-mode captured-key table the host's keyboard router reads. Vim ships as the default flavor; a Kakoune/Helix binding is the same topology with different config, never a fork. Emits are the mechanical vocabulary an editable CodeBlock listens to (SET_MODE / MOTION / OPERATE / INSERT_TEXT) plus one neutral EX_COMMAND for a buffered ':' line — std names no host command; a realization maps EX_COMMAND.name onto its own host vocabulary. A bare EDITOR_FOCUS listen lets every state re-announce its SET_MODE (block caret in NORMAL/VISUAL/OPERATOR_PENDING/COMMAND, bar in INSERT) when the host focuses a different editor surface.

std-modal.name: std-modal
std-modal.description: Modal-only trait: renders ONLY to the `modal` slot. The parent molecule's layout/browse trait is responsible for the `main` slot (the list, the trigger buttons, etc.). Consumers configure icon/title/fields/mode at the trait-ref call site via `config: { ... }`. Side effects (persist, notify) belong in a sibling coordinator trait that `listens { ModalTrait SAVE -> DO_PERSIST }`.

std-multi-party-flow.name: std-multi-party-flow
std-multi-party-flow.description: std-multi-party-flow — Escrow.com / DocuSign / Stripe Connect style multi-party transaction. Header + summary (subject/amount/reference) + named parties (avatar/role/actor) + stage progress + your-turn panel + activity feed + dispute/cancel escape hatches. Topology = loading / awaiting / capturing_dispute / capturing_cancel / funded / released / disputed / cancelled / error.
std-multi-party-flow.statePattern: awaiting, cancelled, capturing_cancel, capturing_dispute, disputed, error, funded, loading, released

std-notification-panel.name: std-notification-panel
std-notification-panel.description: std-notification-panel — the bell's overlay surface. A dedicated modal-only trait that renders the notification list a consumer already passes to std-app-layout's `notifications` knob, and dismisses with a single (render-ui modal null). Mount it beside the app layout and route the layout's notificationClickEvent into OPEN; the catalog trait underneath is never repainted, so opening and closing the bell cannot strand the viewer. Owning the overlay in its own trait is what makes the shape legal — a modal rendered from the trait that also owns `main` is rejected by CIRCUIT_MODAL_EXIT_INCOMPLETE.
std-notification-panel.capabilities: notification overlay, alerts panel, bell dropdown, notification centre, inbox overlay

std-pagination.name: std-pagination
std-pagination.description: std-pagination — single primitive: pagination control. PAGE accepts the Pagination component's `{page}` emit; ITEMS_LOADED accepts an upstream `{data:[ObjectSpec]}` payload and derives totalPages = ceil(len/pageSize). Molecules wire `BrowseItemLoaded -> ITEMS_LOADED` to keep it in lockstep with the data hub.

std-panel-launcher.name: std-panel-launcher
std-panel-launcher.description: std-panel-launcher — a floating button on the page that opens a side panel holding one trait (an assistant, a help panel, a cart). Closed: the button floats bottom-right. Open: the panel shows `contentTrait` under `title` and the button steps aside; the panel's close button (or Escape on small screens) brings the button back. The panel slot defaults to `dock`, which pushes the page aside on wide screens and becomes a side sheet below 1024px. List the trait on every page that should carry the button — it never injects itself.
std-panel-launcher.capabilities: floating action button, launcher, side panel, docked panel, chat launcher, help panel, assistant button

std-pricing.name: std-pricing
std-pricing.description: std-pricing — side-by-side plan cards from a config list: plan name, price and billing period, a one-line summary, the included features, and a link action per plan; one plan can be highlighted as recommended with a badge. Optional heading and footnote. Clicking a plan's action follows its href and emits PLAN_SELECTED. Pick for pricing pages, subscription tiers and service packages.

std-proof.name: std-proof
std-proof.description: std-proof — a marketing section that shows evidence: who uses it, what was made with it, who backs it. `proofLook` picks how: testimonials (portrait, quote, name and role in cards), portfolio (image-led case-study cards that link to the work), logos (a static row of client, sponsor, partner or technology logos), marquee (the same logos or wordmarks with icons gliding past in a continuous strip that pauses on hover and stands still for reduced motion) or badges (name chips, for technologies or certifications without logo images). One `entries` list feeds every look; the heading says what the items are. Carries the same band knobs as the other site sections. Pick for landing, product and campaign pages.

std-prose.name: std-prose
std-prose.description: std-prose — a block of long-form text at a comfortable reading width: optional eyebrow, heading and meta line (date, author), then markdown body with headings, lists, links and code blocks. Supports right-to-left text. Pick for articles, blog posts, about and mission pages, policy text and install notes.

std-rating-review.name: std-rating-review
std-rating-review.description: std-rating-review — Airbnb / Amazon / Google Maps style review surface. Header with aggregate score + Write CTA, per-star distribution bars, working sort chips (recent / top rated / lowest), scrollable reviews list with author + stars + comment + helpful action. Topology = loading / viewing / composing / submitting / submitted / error.
std-rating-review.statePattern: composing, error, loading, submitted, submitting, viewing

std-record-detail.name: std-record-detail
std-record-detail.description: std-record-detail — single primitive: detail-panel. Owns the fetch-one-record state machine (loading → viewing → error, with RETRY), the record counterpart to std-browse's collection machine. Consumers configure fields/sections/actions and the title/subtitle/status bindings; the atom fetches by the id (or, for slug-routed records, the slug) carried on INIT and renders the panel. `detailLook` (panel default / slide-over / page / document) selects the render body, exactly as std-browse's browseLook selects a collection shape.
